A1.justification: Both PDFs describe REP and contain 29 readable pages, including Appendices A-N. Full-text comparison and rendered-page checks establish matching scientific material, with no material gaps limiting comparison.

before.justification: v4.pdf reports original continual-learning experiments measuring accuracy, forgetting, runtime, memory, and energy, including the main comparisons in Table 1 and Jetson TX2 experiments in Appendix M.

after.justification: v6.pdf retains these original experimental results, including the main benchmark comparisons, appendix ablations, and Jetson TX2 energy measurements.

M1.justification: Surrogate prompt selection with random projection, adaptive token merging, and adaptive layer dropping are unchanged. Section 3 and Algorithms 1-2 retain the same procedures and components.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same continual image-classification coverage: CIFAR-100, ImageNet-R, PlantDisease, CUB-200, and subsets of 5-datasets. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main and appendix experiments, including the prompting baselines, acceleration alternatives, adapter methods, CNN methods, F-OAL, and Miro. Table 3's change from Random Drop to random drop is capitalization only.

E3.justification: The reported task splits, batch size of 16, iteration budgets, backbone configurations, metrics, cross-validation, and hardware evaluation procedures are unchanged. The additional task-length and computation-budget experiments were already present in v4.pdf.

E4.justification: Both retain the same component ablations, alternative-algorithm tests, attention and gradient analyses, hyperparameter sensitivity studies, and task-length and computation-budget analyses in Section 3, Section 4.2, and the appendices.

E5.justification: Checklist item 7 identically states that experiments were performed five times and means and standard deviations were reported. The tables retain the same uncertainty reporting, with no added seed information or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and plotted findings in Tables 1-23 and Figures 2-7 are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains REP-L2P with ViT-L on Split ImageNet-R at 75.3 ± 1.5% accuracy, 240 ms iteration time, and 4.5 GB memory.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives, and scheduling equations in Section 3 and Appendix B are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same REP contributions and claims about resource efficiency, accuracy trade-offs, and applicability beyond prompting. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and interpretations of the results are unchanged. Both retain the same qualifications concerning predefined task order, curriculum learning, hyperparameter tuning, replay/privacy, and potential societal harms.

D1.justification: Pseudocode, implementation settings, hardware specifications, power-measurement procedures, and statements about supplying code as a supplementary ZIP remain unchanged. The revised funding acknowledgements add no technical or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix J, and all 45 cited works are retained without changes in research positioning. References 18 and 40 merely move to subsequent pages following acknowledgement reflow.

P1.justification: Table 3 changes Random Drop to random drop and drop ratio to drop ratios. The acknowledgements add an IITP ML-compiler grant and replace an NRF grant identifier; the arXiv version/date stamp also changes. The narrative and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 3 has small caption and internal-heading edits, and the expanded acknowledgements cause local reflow across pages 11-13. Figure designs and table structures remain unchanged; all appendix pages are pixel-identical in the rendered comparison.

improvement.justification: v6.pdf makes small wording and funding-acknowledgement updates, with accompanying reference reflow. The methods, experimental evidence, interpretations, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged throughout both PDFs and their appendices. These localized edits do not establish a meaningful overall quality difference.
